sources.note: Compresses a safety guard's textual rationales into continuous latent states by a staged curriculum, cutting 268 reasoning tokens to 1.60 and latency 8.9-fold, and adds an on-demand decoder that reconstructs a human-readable audit artifact — whose own ablation shows the artifact is anchored far more by the source text than by the latent states it is supposed to inspect.
sources.title: LatentGuard: Efficient and Inspectable Latent Reasoning for LLM Safeguards

sources.note: Automates the hijacking of a reasoning model's own safety reasoning by using a weaker, less-aligned model to simulate execution reasoning and refining attacks from patterns leaked in refusals.
sources.title: AutoRAN: Automated Hijacking of Safety Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models

instructions:
Write the wiki definition for 'HarmBench'.

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

result.definition: A benchmark of harmful behaviour prompts used for red-teaming, appearing in both sources as the adversarial half of a safety evaluation. One includes it among the nine moderation benchmarks over which a guard model's weighted F1 is reported. The other uses it as a source of harmful requests in an automated attack that hijacks a reasoning model's own safety reasoning. The pairing is the archive's usual shape for a safety benchmark: the same prompts serve as the test a defence must pass and as the material an attack is built from.
